venue.name: Kitty Coleman Woodland Gardens
venue.description: Kitty Coleman Woodland Gardens is a privately owned 24 acre woodland garden about 15 minutes north of Courtenay, just off the Old Island Highway. Over a mile of bark mulch paths runs through the forest past ponds, water features and more than 3,000 rhododendrons, with benches, a gazebo, a picnic area and a tea room along the way. It is open year round from 9 a.m. to dusk, and admission is $8 for adults, $3 for children aged 5 to 12 and free for under fives. Guided tours can be prearranged and group reservations can be arranged one day in advance.
restrictions: Dogs on leash are welcome in the gardens.
Good walking shoes and comfortable clothing are recommended.
venue.hours_notes: 9 a.m. to dusk daily. After hours arrangements are available.
venue.seasonal_notes: The gardens are open year round. The rhododendrons bloom mainly from March to the end of June.

programs.name: Group visit
programs.description: The gardens are open daily from 9 a.m. to dusk and group reservations can be arranged one day in advance. Everyone pays the standard admission of $8 for adults, $3 for children aged 5 to 12 and nothing for under fives. No group rate, group size limit or school rate is published, and the site does not say whether adults coming with a group pay.
programs.what_children_do: Walk over a mile of soft bark mulch paths looping through 24 acres of forest, past several ponds, water features and thousands of rhododendrons. There are rustic benches to stop at, a gazebo with bird feeders hung around it, and a stone labyrinth to follow.
programs.our_note: The whole visit is outdoors on bark paths with no stated shelter, so pick a dry day and put the group in boots. Washrooms are not mentioned anywhere on the site, so make that the first thing you ask about on the phone.
programs.practical_summary: There is a picnic area, a gazebo and a tea room, and the gardens are open every day from 9 a.m. to dusk. Washrooms, rain shelter, stroller access and coach parking are not stated, so it is worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: Admission is $8 for adults, $3 for children aged 5 to 12, and free for children under 5. No group or school rate is published.
programs.evidence: Group reservations can be arranged one day in advance.

programs.name: Prearranged guided tour
programs.description: The visitor information page says guided tours can be prearranged. No price, length, group size, age range or minimum notice is published for a tour, and there is no separate page describing one. The one day notice printed on the site is written against group reservations rather than against tours.
programs.our_note: Nothing about the tour is published apart from the fact that you can arrange one. Ask what it costs, how long it runs and whether the guide is used to young children, all in the same call.
programs.practical_summary: Same site as a plain visit, so a picnic area, a gazebo and a tea room, and paths that are outdoors throughout. Price, length and group size for a tour are not published, so phone before you plan the day.
programs.extra_fees_note: No price is published for a guided tour. It is not stated whether the $8 and $3 admission is included, extra, or replaced by a tour fee.

gaps: The site never mentions schools, classes, daycares or children's groups anywhere, so whether they take them is unanswered. Silence is not a no.
No washrooms are mentioned anywhere on the site, including on the visitor information page and the garden map. Ask before you bring a group.
No group rate or school rate is published. The $8 adult and $3 child prices are the general public rates and carry no year, so confirm them before you budget.
Whether adults coming with a group pay full admission is not stated, and no free adult allowance is published.
Guided tours are offered but no price, length, group size, age range or minimum notice is published for them. The one day notice on the site is written against group reservations, not tours.
Stroller and wheelchair access is not addressed. The paths are bark mulch through woodland and the site recommends good walking shoes.
No rain shelter is stated for a booked group. There is a gazebo and a tea room but the site does not say either is available to a group.
Coach and bus parking is not stated. The garden map marks a main entrance parking area but says nothing about vehicle size.
Youngest age welcomed is not stated. Under fives get in free, which is a price and not a policy on age.

Coordinates are the GPS position the gardens publish as text on their own contact page, not a map pin. The map link on that page carries a viewport centre of 49.788294, -125.004626, which agrees with it.
Prices and hours were read from the visitor information page, whose own footer dates it to June 2025. The contact page footer dates to June 2021.
The Artisans Festival advertised for September 5 to 7, 2026 at a $10 entrance fee falls on and just before the date of this check, so that fee applies to that weekend only and not to a normal visit.
